root_cause.mechanism: clang (LLVM) writes every -o object through a TempFile whose fd stays OPEN across rename(temp -> final) and is closed AFTERWARDS. fat16_rename correctly deletes the temp's 0x0F run + short entry and allocates the final entry (often REUSING the just-freed slot). The LATER close of the still-open temp fd then ran fat16_sync_entry (dirty) and wrote the stale cached temp dirent back over that slot: (a) the temp's mangled 8.3 alias ('CPU-09EF.O.T' = format_83 of the long temp name 'cpu-<hex>.o.tmp') resurfaces as a duplicate twin pointing at the same data cluster, and (b) when the rename's clean entry had reused the slot it got CLOBBERED -> only the twin survives, lld cannot open nfs_test.o / cpu.o.
root_cause.why_not_seen_in_older_tests: existing fat16 tests close the write handle BEFORE renaming; none exercised rename-while-open-then-close (the LLVM TempFile order).
root_cause.determinism: filename-keyed because the slot reuse/clobber pattern depends deterministically on allocation order, per fork burst not address layout.

failing_test.what: creates CPU.O + NFS_TEST.O plus 45 object names via create(long TempFile name)->write->rename-while-open->close (the clang order), then asserts EXACTLY one clean dirent per final name and open-by-clean-name with written size 2048.
failing_test.on_tip: FAIL (Tests run 319, failed 1): the close-after-rename resurrected the temp alias; the exactly-one-clean-dirent check failed.

fix.summary: before writing a dirty entry back at close, read the on-disk slot at (dir_sector, dir_offset) and SKIP when the slot was freed (0x00/0xE5 by a rename/unlink under this open handle) or now holds a different file's 11-byte name (slot reused by the rename's clean entry). A handle whose entry a rename deleted must not resurrect it.
fix.coverage: also guards the synthetic-root handle (dir_sector==0) and generalizes the existing 'read descriptor must not clobber' intent to stale WRITE handles.
